digest.component_or_area: Cloud adapter (Jira) — 429 retry behavior, config validation, and probe configuration
propositions: Cloud's per-member 429 sweep must enumerate every mutating transport member classified by both transport seam (ACLI subprocess, pooled REST, or bare urlopen) and dispatch level (retrying wrapper, non-retrying apply phases, or no wrapper) with duplicate-write assessment recorded in a repo-artifact table, testing attempt count at each member's own 429 boundary rather than merely that an exception escapes.

Cloud must reject non-HTTPS base URLs with a config validation failure or the test must record that it deliberately does not, and a linked bug filed if rejection is absent; missing credentials must fail loudly on backend construction rather than silently proceeding (bug cd78 shape) or a linked bug filed if the silent path exists.

Cloud's probe.RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES is a hardcoded frozenset while DC reads resolved_statuses from config; the decision must be recorded as a repo-artifact comment stating whether a Cloud deployment using non-standard workflow state names requires a runtime config hook (warranting a follow-up ticket) or whether the constant suffices.

Every mutating Cloud transport member reached through dispatch_one._call_with_retry must be asserted to retry on 429 with bounded attempt count and Retry-After honoring, while members in non-retrying dispatch_apply_phases paths must assert exactly one attempt at that boundary.

Pooled-REST and bare-urlopen mutating members (acli_cli_ops.update_priority confirmed) invoked directly on the transport must assert exactly one attempt under a 429 at the shared process-wide urllib.request.urlopen boundary.

Subprocess-seam mutating members must assert the bounded Retry-After backoff retry in _run_acli rather than one attempt, and any mutation retried on 429 at an undocumented layer must trigger a linked bug (the two known deliberate retries do not trigger bugs by themselves).
